Done. `out/T4/model.safetensors` is written, in one execution with no failures.

**Approach:** a plain script (`out/T4/solution.py`) on `safetensors` 0.5.3 + `torch` 2.14.0. I deliberately did not use mergekit's `task_arithmetic`: it applies the scaled task vectors to every tensor, so it can't express "touch only these 48 MLP tensors, copy the other 66 bit-exactly", and it offers no place to assert the frozen-backbone precondition before writing.

**What the script does:**
- Opens the base through `model.safetensors.index.json` (it's sharded; the fine-tunes are single files), lazily via `safe_open` so the three ~5 GB checkpoints are never all resident.
- Verifies, before writing anything: identical 114-name key sets across all three; matching shape/dtype per tensor; `torch.equal(base, ft1)` and `torch.equal(base, ft2)` for each of the 66 non-MLP tensors.
- Merges the 48 MLP tensors (matched by an anchored regex, count asserted) in float32, with **both** task vectors taken against the same unmodified base tensor.
- Asserts 48 merged and 114 output tensors, writes to a `.tmp` path and renames, then reopens the file and re-asserts the count and names.

Every check raises and exits non-zero, so the run fails loudly if any does not hold.

**Independent verification** (separate script, not part of the solution): all 66 non-MLP tensors bit-identical to the base, all 48 merged tensors within 1e-6 relative Frobenius error of the specified formula, shapes and dtypes preserved.

Self-report is at `out/T4/REPORT.md`. Runtime was 13 s.
